findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data at rest.

No acl attribute or aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is set for this bucket, leaving access control at the provider/account default rather than explicitly enforcing private access and blocking public ACLs/policies.
This bucket stores financial ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket despite storing model artifacts, exposing them to unauthorized access if the bucket or underlying storage is ever exposed.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational runbook data (which may contain internal infrastructure details or credentials) is stored unencrypted at rest.

The object is uploaded without specifying server_side_encryption or kms_key_id and is placed into a bucket (reports_archive) that itself lacks default encryption, so this potentially sensitive vendor roster file is stored unencrypted.
